name: Expulsion Science
_comment_group: One more show under the Snapchat heading, cut to Hall of Femme's
design. Everything that makes it a Snapchat pack is Hall of Femme's
and is taken from the same presets rather than restated: the frame
fetch, the 540x960 vertical output, the transcription, the rewrite
that turns speech into report, the stated 40px, the twenty characters
to a line, the freeform text box, the drag.
What makes it a different show is the face and the colour. It is set
in Montserrat Bold, in one purple, with picked words in Montserrat
ExtraBold - and with no card under any of it, which is the one place
it parts company with the pack it was cut from and the one place that
costs more than a value. That is argued below.
The id is kebab-case ASCII because it is also the folder name and the
key everything else refers to; the name is the brand.
_comment_capture: The frame fetch, whole, from content/presets/snapchat-capture.json:
the slider's range, the 540x960 output, the transcription, and the
rewrite that turns it from speech into report. This channel has
nothing to say about any of it that its neighbours do not.
_comment_title: The whole of the difference between this show and Hall of Femme.
Set in Montserrat Bold, in #665282, with picked words in Montserrat
ExtraBold and no card behind the block. Everything else - the size,
where the lines break, the capitals, the freeform box, the drag, the
margin off the foot of the frame - is the Snapchat caption design and
Two things this pack overrides in that preset, and the second follows
from the first. The card is dropped, so the type is over the
photograph; therefore the drop shadow comes back, because that is
what holds type legible over a photograph nobody chose the contrast
of. The highlight is NOT promoted to a box along with it, and that is
a deliberate departure from what Conspiracy Central did on dropping
its own card - see the highlight note, which is where the cost of it
is written down rather than hidden.
Uppercased, inherited, for the reason every pack under this heading
is: at 40px with twenty characters to a line the caption is three
short beats rather than a paragraph, and capitals are what those are
set in. Montserrat has no lower case anybody would call the brand,
and its capitals are geometric enough to carry a line of them.

_comment_color: The one colour this show is set in, on every frame, for good.
Unlike Hall of Femme it offers no palette (see below), so this is
THE colour rather than the colour a frame opens on.
It is a mid-dark purple, which on a card would be an unremarkable
choice and over a photograph is the reason the shadow below is
stated. Nothing else in the frame is this show's: no card, no
box, no second colour at a picked word. One purple and a weight
step is the whole of the brand, so the purple has to be the
purple - it is not adjusted to suit a background, because there
is no background for it to be adjusted against.
_comment_shadow: Back, and this is the one sentence in the preset this pack
contradicts. Every channel under this heading sets `shadow` to
null, on the argument that a drop shadow is what keeps type
legible over a photograph nobody chose the contrast of and there
is no photograph under those letters - there is a solid card
The argument is right, and it is exactly why dropping the card
means picking the shadow back up. There IS a photograph under
these letters, on all forty stills. A purple this deep is worse
off than the near-white Conspiracy Central hangs over its frames:
white only disappears into the bright end of a picture, where
#665282 has a dark end and a bright end to lose itself in, and a
captured still is whatever the video happened to be showing.
The numbers are the skeleton's own (see BASE_TITLE_STYLE.shadow
in js/channels.js) rather than a fresh set invented here. They
are what every channel that sets type on a photograph in this app
uses, which is the same job this is; a pack with no reason of its
own should not carry a number it merely agrees with, and where it
has to state one anyway it should state the one already in use.
_comment_colors: Absent, and worth the note because the pack this one was cut from
is the pack that INVENTED the feature - sixteen pairings of four
colours in two rows of swatches - and anyone reading the two side
by side will look for it here.
Two of the three rows could not be drawn even if somebody wanted
them. `colors.panel` needs a panel and there is none (see the
note on `colors` in js/channels.js), and `colors.highlight` needs
a highlight that IS a colour, where this one is a weight.
That leaves `colors.text`, and a list with one colour in it is a
row holding a single swatch that is already the answer: a button
that visibly does nothing, which is the one kind of control this
panel does not have anywhere (see the note on paletteOf in
js/editor.js). This show has one colour, so it states it as its
colour and not as its only option. If it is ever given a second,
the row is one line here and costs nothing to bring back.
_comment_highlight: A picked word is set in Montserrat ExtraBold, in the same colour
as the rest of the block. The highlight here is WEIGHT, exactly
as it is on Hall of Femme: the colour it names is the block's, so
the recolour draws what its neighbours are drawn in and the face
is the whole of the difference. Stated all the same, for the
fallback reason `color` above is stated - a highlight that
changed colour as well as weight would be two highlights.
What is worth being plain about is how much smaller the step is
here than the one it is copied from. Hall of Femme picks out
words at Telegraf 200 against 800, which is a family's two ends
and is as loud as a box; this is 700 against 800, one cut apart
in a text sans, and it is quieter than any other highlight under
this heading. On Hall of Femme's card that would still read,
because a card is a controlled ground. Over a photograph it is
the smallest signal this app draws.
It is still what the brand asked for, and it is left as asked
rather than rescued with a box. Conspiracy Central dropped its
card and promoted its highlight to a box in the same breath, on
the argument that a recolour of two words in a block of one
colour is two words in that same colour to anyone scrolling. The
argument applies here too - but a box needs a fill colour, a fill
colour is a second brand colour, and this show has one. Inventing
the second to make the first louder would be the pack deciding
what the brand is.
So the entry to change, the day this show wants a highlight that
carries at a scroll, is a `fill` beside a `mode` of box - not the
face, which is the part that was specified.
The mode and the scope come from the preset, and the scope is
worth keeping in view: word rather than line, because a caption's
line breaks are wherever the sentence ran out of width, so
picking a LINE out picks out a fragment rather than a thought.
The shadow is the third thing dropping the card costs, and it is
stated for the same reason `shadow` above is. The preset sets the
highlight's to null because its letters are on a card; these are
not, and a picked word over a photograph needs exactly the lift
its neighbours have. So it takes the block's own numbers rather
than a second set - a picked word here differs from the words
either side of it in weight, and in nothing else. Conspiracy
Central, the other pack under this heading with no card, does the
same.
_comment_panel: No card. This is the decision the rest of the pack is downstream
of, and the two consequences are the `shadow` above and the size
of the highlight beside it.
Stated as null rather than left out, because it cannot be left
out: `use` merges the preset UNDER this pack (see `expand` in
js/channels.js), so the card's shape, padding, corners and shadow
arrive from snapchat-caption.json whatever this pack says about
them. Null is how a pack cut from that preset declines the one
part of it that is a whole shape rather than a number.
One thing changes quietly with it and is easy to miss, and it is
not the margin. `bottomRatio` is measured to the block's own box
rather than to what is drawn (see blockTop0 in js/text.js), so
the box still bottoms out 120px off the foot of the frame here,
exactly as it does on a panelled sibling.
What changes is the box. Under a line-scope panel the card's
padding is inside the band the rows are stacked by, so dropping
the card makes the block SHORTER and the letters come down with
it: measured at two lines of twenty characters, this pack sets
the same sentence twenty pixels lower on the frame than Hall of
Femme does. It also stops anything hanging below the margin,
where the card used to put twelve pixels of padding and a shadow
of its own - so what is drawn ends higher even though the block
sits lower.
The margin is inherited unchanged all the same: 120px off the
foot of a 960-tall frame is measured against the player's own
furniture along the bottom edge, and that furniture does not move
because a card went away.

_comment_branding: No dark gradient, like every pack under this heading - and like
Conspiracy Central this one needs its own sentence, because the usual
reason does not apply. Its siblings say the gradient has nothing to
do: their titles are on a card and not on the photograph. This one's
It still has nothing to do. The backend's gradient is a SIDE gradient
- full height, never past half the width, peaking on whichever side
the title column is (reframe_engine.apply_dark_gradient) - because it
was drawn for a landscape thumbnail with a headline set beside the
subject. There is no title column on a captured still: the block lies
across the width of the frame, and darkening one half of forty
pictures would shade half of every caption and leave the other half
exactly as it was. What holds this type off the photograph is its own
drop shadow, which is the tool for the job at this scale.
